key_insight: JEPA-Anything proposes a single predictive learning principle that can work across very different domains by factorizing what should be predicted into complementary parts. In simple terms, it aims to make world models more general, less domain-specific, and easier to transfer.
problem_solved: Most predictive world models are built for one specific environment or data type, making them hard to reuse across different systems. This paper addresses the challenge of learning a common world-modeling framework that can generalize across radically different domains.
method: Extends joint-embedding predictive architectures with orthogonal predictive factorization (OPF) to split latent targets into complementary factors.
Learns each factor through dedicated prediction pathways, reducing interference between different predictive components.
Uses a domain-agnostic setup so the same learning principle can be applied across multiple worlds or data modalities.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could simplify building reusable predictive models that transfer better across tasks and environments. It may also improve representation learning for agents that need to anticipate outcomes in diverse settings.

paper_title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
